query: I'm a working adult with a full-time job. Should I do my university degree online or in person?
sources:
Source 1 (2023, US News, USA): Online degree programs from accredited universities have largely closed the employer perception gap — major employers including Deloitte, Amazon, and the US federal government no longer distinguish between online and on-campus degrees from the same institution.

Source 2 (2022, Georgetown Center on Education, USA): In-person programs produce stronger professional networks, higher internship conversion rates, and better first-job salaries on average — the social and networking benefits of physical presence are difficult to replicate online.

Source 3 (2023, Reddit r/Online_Education, USA): Community of working adult learners strongly favors online programs for the flexibility to maintain income while studying — many report completing degrees that would have been impossible while working full-time on-campus.

Source 4 (2022, Coursera Industry Report, Global): Online learners complete degrees at significantly lower rates than in-person students — completion requires strong self-discipline and many working adults underestimate the difficulty of balancing work, family, and coursework.

Source 5 (2021, Inside Higher Ed, USA): Hybrid and HyFlex programs now offer a middle ground — students attend some classes in person for high-value interactions while completing most coursework online, combining flexibility with networking benefits.
atoms: perspective: Career-changer focused on networking outcomes
perspective: Full-time worker prioritizing schedule flexibility
plausible_answers: Choose an accredited online degree, since employers now largely treat it equally and preserving your income outweighs networking disadvantages.
Attend in person in networking-driven fields like consulting, finance, or law, since physical presence directly drives career outcomes.
Seek a hybrid or HyFlex program, attending key classes in person to preserve high-value networking that purely online programs miss.
